learning: Iteration 2 showed line loss at zero with s-bend progress at 0.04, so the failure is turn response, not sensing reach. Next, if s-bend progress recovers, separate lead from inertia. If it does not, test kd and base_speed before changing geometry again.
notes: Builder geometry used unchanged (lead 0.05 m, 0.12 x 0.10 m body, 0.6 kg). Controller changes only kd, raised from 0.2 to 0.6, to damp the faster turn response expected from lower yaw inertia. Gains, base speed and weights are otherwise unchanged from iteration 2.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 0 (lead y=0.05 m, track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg) was the best run at 79.6, with s-bend progress 0.29. Iteration 1 (lead 0.03 m, track 0.10 m) and iteration 2 (7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.03 m) both fell, to 56.2 and 39.5. In iteration 2 line loss fell to 0 on the oval and s-bend, yet s-bend progress collapsed to 0.04 and max_error stayed at about 0.061 m. So the robot leaves the line on bends it can still see, which points to overshoot or too little damping rather than sensing. The Builder's package restores the lead to y=0.05 m and cuts yaw inertia by about 45 percent (mass 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m). Lower inertia makes the robot turn faster for the same command, so it can overshoot more. I therefore keep kp 2.0 and base_speed 1.4 unchanged so the Builder's change is what is tested, and raise kd from 0.2 to 0.6 to damp the faster turn response. Sensor weights stay proportional to sensor x (about 1 per 30 mm), so the signal stays within the +/-2 limit, and line_loss stays 'last_direction', which gave the best result so far. Expected: s-bend progress rising toward 0.25 or more and steering_oscillation rising only modestly. This is a judgement based on the evidence above, not a measured result. Risk: with kd up, edge jitter from the 7-sensor array may increase.
